parts.text: Obadiah announces judgment on Edom, whose mountain strongholds have fostered pride. Neither height, allies, wisdom, nor warriors will save it. Its guilt lies especially in violence against its brother Jacob: Edom rejoiced over Jerusalem’s distress, shared in its plunder, intercepted fugitives, and handed survivors to their enemies.

The day of the LORD approaches for all nations, and their deeds will return upon their own heads. In contrast, Mount Zion will have deliverance and holiness, and Jacob will recover its inheritance. The houses of Jacob and Joseph are pictured as fire consuming Esau’s stubble. Returning captives regain territories, deliverers judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom belongs to the LORD.
